# Ebay (2 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /search | `query` | 5 | Search eBay listings |
| /product | `product_id` | 5 | Get an eBay listing by item id |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /search — 5cr

Returns eBay listings matching a keyword, 60 per page on an active search, each with its item id, title, price, original price where the listing is discounted, currency, condition, image, seller handle, seller feedback percentage and count, units sold, buying format, and the listing URL. Pass show_only=sold_items for sold listings: price is the realised sale and product.ext.sold_at is the sold date. completed_items returns all ended listings. Callers never supply an eBay login or cookie. Feed a returned item id into GET /v1/ebay/product for the full listing including seller reputation depth. When crawling, note that the result total eBay reports is an estimate that changes between pages, so it is not returned here: paginate until a page comes back empty.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Free-text listing search, for example airpods pro or vintage seiko.
- `country` *(optional)*: eBay marketplace as a two-letter country code: US (ebay.com, default), GB, AU, CA, DE, FR, IT, ES, IE, AT, CH, NL, BE, PL, SG, MY, PH, HK, or MX. The marketplace sets the listing pool, language, and currency.
- `page` *(optional)*: Page number, starting at 1. Prefer the universal cursor parameter. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort_by` *(optional)*: Result ordering: best_match (default), price_low, price_high, newly_listed, or ending_soonest.
- `condition` *(optional)*: Restrict to one item condition: new, opened_box, refurbished, or used.
- `buying_format` *(optional)*: Restrict to one sale type: auction, buy_it_now, or accepts_offers.
- `show_only` *(optional)*: Restrict results. sold_items returns listings that ended in a sale (price is the realised sale; product.ext.sold_at is the sold date). completed_items returns all ended listings, including those that did not sell. Combine with a comma, for example sold_items,completed_items. free_shipping is also accepted. No eBay login or cookie is required.
- `min_price` *(optional)*: Lowest price to include. Applied by eBay and approximate, so filter on product.price.current if you need a hard bound.
- `max_price` *(optional)*: Highest price to include. Applied by eBay and approximate, so filter on product.price.current if you need a hard bound.
- `aspects` *(optional)*: Category-specific item aspect filter taken from a previous response, for example Brand:Apple.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `page` (page style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/ebay/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /product — 5cr

Returns full detail for a single eBay listing: title, brand, price, original price, currency, condition and condition notes, MPN and UPC, units available, units sold, watchers, and the seller. The seller block is the reason to call this rather than search: product.ext.seller_reputation carries lifetime feedback percentage and count, top-rated status, items sold, join date, and four detailed sub-ratings for description accuracy, shipping cost, shipping speed, and communication. One known gap: eBay's detail response currently returns a corrupt image array, so image_urls is null here. Use the image on the matching GET /v1/ebay/search row, which is unaffected.

**Parameters**

- `product_id`: eBay item id, the numeric id in a listing URL: ebay.com/itm/327256602116 is item id 327256602116. Item ids also come back on every row of GET /v1/ebay/search.
- `country` *(optional)*: eBay marketplace as a two-letter country code: US (ebay.com, default), GB, AU, CA, DE, FR, IT, ES, IE, AT, CH, NL, BE, PL, SG, MY, PH, HK, or MX. The marketplace sets the listing pool, language, and currency.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/ebay/product?product_id=<product_id>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing an eBay endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Search listings for a keyword | `/search` | 5 |
| One listing by item id | `/product` | 5 |

Two endpoints, both 5 credits. eBay's value in research is **resale price discovery** — what
people actually pay for a thing right now, rather than what a retailer lists it at. That makes
`/search` (5cr) the more useful of the two: a spread of live listings tells you more than one
listing does.

Because there is no 1cr rung, avoid exploratory querying. Frame the search once.
